tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a larger disk that must be moved is not the topmost disk on its peg, first relocate any smaller disks that sit above it to other pegs. This clears the larger disk so it can be moved legally.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that is buried under smaller disks on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk while smaller disks remain on top of it, resulting in an illegal move because the larger disk is not the topmost.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before executing a move, verify that the chosen disk is actually the topmost disk on its source peg. Moving any other disk violates the Tower of Hanoi rules.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before every move in the generated sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 from a peg where disk 2 is on top, causing an illegal move because disk 5 is not the topmost.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure the destination peg is empty or its topmost disk is larger than the disk being moved. Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one is prohibited.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Immediately after confirming the source disk, before committing the move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 3 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2, creating a larger‑on‑smaller violation.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Use the standard recursive algorithm: to move k disks from source to target, first move k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the kth disk, then move the k‑1 disks from auxiliary to target. This yields a concise, correct sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a contiguous stack of disks from one peg to another.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Generating a move list by moving disks in an ad‑hoc order, which leads to missing or extra moves and an incorrect final configuration.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg currently has a smaller disk on top, move that smaller disk elsewhere before placing the larger disk. This prevents illegal larger‑on‑smaller placement.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you intend to move a larger disk onto a peg that already contains disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top, violating the size rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate final configuration after move generation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, simulate the moves from the initial state and verify that the resulting configuration exactly matches the goal. This catches missing or misordered moves before submission.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After the entire move sequence has been generated, just before output.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing a move list that leaves disk 5 on the wrong peg, so the final configuration does not match the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use the smallest disk as a flexible temporary placeholder
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any larger disk or an empty peg without restriction, making it ideal for temporarily holding other disks while larger ones are moved.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a temporary holder to free other disks and the smallest disk is available.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Getting stuck because the smallest disk was never used as a temporary holder, leading to a deadlock with no legal moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place move list as the final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Output the move list as the very last list in the response, without any surrounding text, code fences, or additional brackets, so the verifier extracts the correct sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including explanatory text after the move list, causing the parser to read the later text as the answer and ignore the actual moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Keep move list concise to avoid token limit truncation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a short, near‑optimal sequence (e.g., using recursion) rather than an overly long list, to stay within the model’s output token limit and prevent truncation.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move sequence, especially for larger numbers of disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Producing a very long move list that gets cut off, resulting in an incomplete solution.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Ensure non‑empty move list when moves are required
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the initial configuration does not already match the goal, the generated move list must contain at least one legal move; an empty list indicates a failure to solve the problem.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After checking whether the initial state equals the goal, before outputting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Returning [] (empty list) for a problem where disks need to be rearranged, leading to an incorrect solution.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume the puzzle is already solved or fail to generate any moves when the initial configuration differs from the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check whether the initial state matches the goal; if not, generate at least one legal move and ensure the move list is not empty before output.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The generated move sequence exceeds the model’s output token limit, causing the list to be cut off.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the move list concise by using recursive strategies that produce near‑optimal sequences, staying well within the token budget.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk that is buried under other disks on its source peg, violating the rule that only the topmost disk can be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, verify that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model attempts to place a larger disk on top of a smaller one, breaking the size ordering rule.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before executing the move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Extra list after move list causing parser to read wrong answer
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model includes additional text or another list after the move list, leading the verifier to parse the wrong segment as the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Output the move list as the very last list in the response, with no trailing text or extra brackets.
